title: Dandelion leaf infusion for water retention
subtitle: A gentle diuretic tea of dried dandelion leaf for premenstrual bloating and fluid retention
excerpt: Dandelion leaf infusion is a simple hot tea brewed from dried Taraxacum officinale leaf, traditionally taken for the bloating and water retention that accompany the premenstrual week. Unlike pharmaceutical diuretics, the leaf is rich in potassium and does not deplete the mineral it is traditionally used for. One to two cups a day for a few days, brewed fresh each time.

glossaryTerms.definition: A herb or preparation that increases urine output and supports the clearance of excess fluid from the body. Dandelion leaf is unusual in also being high in potassium, which ordinary diuretics deplete.

content.text: Dandelion leaf infusion is a hot tea of dried Taraxacum officinale leaf steeped for 8 minutes and drunk before the worst of the bloating. A gentle

traditionally taken for the fluid retention and abdominal fullness of the premenstrual week. What makes it unusual among diuretics, herbal or pharmaceutical, is that dandelion leaf is itself a significant source of potassium, partly replacing what any diuretic preparation removes. The taste is mildly bitter and vegetal. One to two cups a day during the week before a period, then stop.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor before use. Full precautions are in the 'When not to use' section.

content.text: Place 2 teaspoons of dried dandelion leaf in a teapot or heatproof cup.
Pour 200 ml of just-boiled water over the herb. Cover and steep for 8 minutes.
Strain into a cup and drink warm. Honey or a slice of lemon improves the taste.
One to two cups a day during the premenstrual week. Take in the morning rather than at bedtime, the diuretic effect is gentle but real. Stop once the period begins and the bloating clears.
Dried dandelion leaf stores 12 months in a sealed tin away from light and heat. Prepare each cup fresh.
When not to use this remedy

Do not take alongside prescribed diuretics without advice from your prescriber. See a doctor for persistent fluid retention, ankle or face swelling, or bloating that does not go away. These may indicate heart, kidney, or liver conditions.
